title: His Childhood Friend Ruined My Car, I Ruined His Empire
synopsis: Delia Vance hides her true identity as heir of the almighty Vance family and lives as an ordinary high school student. Her father arranges an engagement with elite school golden boy Grayson Hale. At the parking lot, Grayson’s friend Tiffany bullies her, demands huge compensation and threatens her. Everyone mocks Delia as a nobody. When an armored convoy arrives, her real status shocks the whole crowd. She smashes the arrogance of the Hale family effortlessly.
intro: Delia Vance lives as an ordinary high school student, and nobody at the elite school knows she is heir to the almighty Vance family. It reads like a hidden-identity romance novel, now on screen: an arranged engagement to golden boy Grayson Hale, a parking-lot standoff with his friend Tiffany, and a crowd that has already decided Delia is a nobody. The payoff is the moment an armored convoy rolls in and everyone finally sees who she is.
why: A hidden-heiress setup where the audience knows her real status long before the bullies do.
A school-and-engagement story with a clear villain to root against.
Good pick if you like quiet heroines who let the arrogant dig their own hole before the reveal.

faq.q: Is His Childhood Friend Ruined My Car, I Ruined His Empire worth watching?
faq.a: If you enjoy hidden identities and bullies getting put in their place, yes. It is built around one big reveal and the fallout for the Hale family.
Delia Vance, the hidden heir of the Vance family; Grayson Hale, the school golden boy she is engaged to; and Tiffany, his friend who bullies her in the parking lot.
